keckle.c: KECKLE, when the Gabies of a Ship do Gatile in the Hawse, or the Bolt-ropes do so against the Ships Quarter, the Seamen wind some small Ropes about them, and this serving of these Ropes is called Keckling.

keel.c: KEEL, is the lowest Piece of Timber in a Ship, in the Bottom of her Hull; one end whereof is at the Stem, the other at the Stem, into this are all the Ground-Timbers and Hooks fastened, and bolted Fore and Aft. When a Ship hath a deep Keel, slie is said to have a Rank Keel, and this serves well to keep her from Rowling ; but if Ihe is over floaty and Rowls too much, a new Keel is sometimes put on called, a False Keel.

keeperofthegreatseal.c: KEEPER of the Great-Seal, is a Lord by his Office, and stiled Lord Keeper of the Great-Seal of England : He is one of the King’s Privy-Council ; through whose Hands pass all Charters, Commissions, and Grants of the King under the Great Seal-, without which Seal, all such Instruments by Law are of no force. For the King is (in the Interpretation of Law, a Corporation, and passeth nothing firmly but under the laid Seal, which is as the Publick Faith of the Kingdom, in the high Esteem and Reputation justly attributed thereto. This Lord Keeper hath the same Place, Authority, Preheminence, Jurisdiction, Execution of Laws, and-ail ether Customs, Commodities and Advantages, as the Lord Chancellor of England hath for the time being. He is constituted by the Delivery of the Great-Seal to him, and taking his Oath.

keeperoftheprivyseal.c: KEEPER of the Privy-Ssal, is a Lord by his Office, through whose Hands pass all Charters signed by the King, before they come to the Great-Seal, and some things which do not pass the Great-Seal at all. He is of the King's Privy council, and one of the Great Officers of the Kingdom
